name: ADUM120N1BRZ-RL7
title: 3.0 kV rms dual-channel digital isolators
summary: ADuM120N and ADuM121N: two-channel digital isolators in an 8-lead narrow SOIC with 3 kV rms withstand, passing logic across a transformer barrier by on/off keying of a carrier. The ADuM120N carries both channels one way, the ADuM121N one each way. Each side runs from 1.7 V to 5.5 V, so the part also shifts logic levels; data rate is at least 150 Mbps and delay at most 13 ns at 5 V. The N0 and N1 versions differ in the output level they fall to when the input side loses power: low or high.
key_figures: 3000 V rms for 1 min (UL 1577); VIORM 565 V peak
1.7 V to 5.5 V on each side
13 ns max at 5 V, 15 ns max at 1.8 V

circuits.title: Recommended PCB layout
circuits.description: The isolator with one decoupling capacitor on each side and nothing else: C1 from VDD1 (pin 1) to GND1 (pin 4), C2 from VDD2 (pin 8) to GND2 (pin 5). The two logic inputs and two outputs connect straight to the logic they serve with no interface parts. Each capacitor is 0.01 µF to 0.1 µF, with no more than 10 mm of total lead length between its two ends and the supply pin.
notes: The ADuM121N takes the same two capacitors on the same pins; only its pins 2 and 7 swap direction.

where.VDC: dc component of the working voltage

equations.note: Example: 240 V rms line on one side and a 400 V dc bus on the other give VRMS = sqrt(240^2 + 400^2) = 466 V, the figure used with material group and pollution degree to find the creepage a system standard requires.

where.tPHL: propagation delay to a logic low output, 50% input to 50% output

operation.text: Two-channel digital isolators, 3 kV rms. The ADuM120N passes both channels from side 1 to side 2; the ADuM121N passes channel B from side 1 to side 2 and channel A from side 2 to side 1. The digit after N sets the output state when the input side is unpowered or disabled: N0 parts go low, N1 parts go high. Pin compatibility: ADuM120N0 with ADuM1285; ADuM120N1 with ADuM1280 and ADuM1200; ADuM121N0 with ADuM1286; ADuM121N1 with ADuM1281 and ADuM1201.

Each channel drives a chip-scale air-core transformer, its coils separated by polyimide layers, with a high-frequency carrier switched on and off by the data (on/off keying) over a differential path; a receiver on the far side demodulates it and an output buffer drives the pin. On N0 parts the carrier is off while the input is low; on N1 parts it is off while the input is high. When the input side is off or not operating, N0 outputs go low and N1 outputs go high. The output is correct at dc with no input edges. Each side has its own internal regulator. The carrier is spread-spectrum to lower radiated emissions.

Each side runs from 1.7 V to 5.5 V independently, so the part translates between 1.8 V, 2.5 V, 3.3 V and 5 V logic. Input thresholds and output levels follow the supply of their own side (VDDx). Input signal edges may be as slow as 1.0 ms.

Each supply has a lockout: typically rising threshold 1.6 V, falling threshold 1.5 V, 0.1 V hysteresis. With the input side unpowered the outputs sit at their fail-safe level; with the output side unpowered they are indeterminate.
Logic inputs on a side whose supply is off must be held low; a high input would feed that side through the ESD protection structures.

Bypass both supplies: one capacitor from pin 1 to pin 4 for VDD1 and one from pin 8 to pin 5 for VDD2, each 0.01 µF to 0.1 µF. Total lead length from either capacitor end to the supply pin is 10 mm at most. The logic pins need no external interface parts. Analog Devices application note AN-1109 covers layout further.

Under large common-mode transients, board capacitance across the barrier should be small, and what remains should couple equally to all pins on one side. Unequal coupling can drive pin-to-pin voltages past the absolute maximum ratings, with latch-up or permanent damage as the result.

Propagation delay runs from the input's 50% point to the output's 50% point and can differ for a rising and a falling output (tPLH, tPHL). Pulse width distortion is the largest difference between those two delays. Channel matching is the largest delay difference between the channels of one part; propagation delay skew is the largest delay difference between parts under the same conditions.
Jitter figures come from an eye diagram at 150 Mbps, pseudorandom bit sequence with n = 14, 5 V supplies; a typical part shows 380 ps p-p.

Insulation fails in two ways: surface tracking, which sets creepage in system standards and depends on the rms working voltage, pollution degree and material group (material group II, 4.0 mm creepage for this package), and wear-out, driven by displacement current in the polyimide. Only the ac part of the voltage across the barrier causes wear-out; dc causes very little. The ac limits in the maximum continuous working voltage table apply to the ac rms part given by the working voltage equations. The dc limit in that table is set by package creepage per IEC 60664-1 and can differ under a given system standard.
8-lead narrow-body SOIC (R-8), RoHS compliant, JEDEC MS-012-AA. Dimensions are controlled in millimetres.
